function.name: read_file
function.description: Read the contents of a file. Optionally specify a 1-based line range. If append_loc is true, each line is prefixed with its line number (e.g. "1→...").

end_line.description: Last line to read, 1-based inclusive (default: end of file)

append_loc.description: Prefix each line with its line number

function.name: file_glob_search
function.description: Recursively search for files matching a glob pattern under a directory. Automatically skips files ignored by .gitignore (when the directory is inside a git repo) and common junk directories (.git, node_modules, build, dist, etc.) otherwise. A pattern with no '/' (e.g. "*.cpp") matches the file's basename at any depth. A pattern containing '/' matches the full relative path; unless already anchored with "**/" or a leading '/', it is automatically prefixed with "**/". Use type="dir" or "all" to also list directories; directory entries are suffixed with '/' in the output. Note: directory listings do not apply .gitignore filtering.

include.description: Glob pattern for files to include (e.g. "*.cpp" or "src/**/*.cpp"). Default: **

exclude.description: Glob pattern for files to exclude

max_depth.description: Maximum depth to descend into subdirectories (default: 0 = unlimited; 1 = direct children only)

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return, capped at 100 (default 100)

function.name: grep_search
function.description: Search for a pattern in files under a path. Returns matching lines with file paths (and, unless searching a single file, paths relative to the given directory). Automatically skips files ignored by .gitignore (when the directory is inside a git repo) and common junk directories (.git, node_modules, build, dist, etc.) otherwise. include/exclude: a pattern with no '/' matches the basename at any depth; a pattern containing '/' matches the full relative path (auto-anchored with "**/" unless already anchored).

path.description: File or directory to search in

pattern.description: Pattern to search for (regular expression unless literal is true)

return_line_numbers.description: If true, include line numbers in results

literal.description: Treat pattern as a literal string instead of a regular expression (default: false)

context_lines.description: Number of lines of context to show before and after each match (default: 0)

function.name: exec_shell_command
function.description: Execute a shell command and return its output (stdout and stderr combined).

function.name: write_file
function.description: Write content to a file, creating it (including parent directories) if it does not exist. May use with edit_file for more complex edits.

path.description: Path of the file to write

function.name: edit_file
function.description: Edit a file using exact text replacement. Each edits[].old_text must be unique in the file and is matched against the original content, not incrementally. Merge nearby changes into one edit instead of overlapping edits. Use write_file to replace the whole file.

path.description: Path to the file to edit

edits.description: One or more exact text replacements to apply

old_text.description: Exact text to find; must be unique in the file and must not overlap with other edits

function.name: get_info
function.description: Returns runtime info: the OS name/version and the current working directory

function.name: local_dictate_once
function.description: Listen to one utterance on the Pi's USB headset and return the Moonshine transcription

function.name: local_search_notes
function.description: Semantically search the user's saved memory notes -- prior project decisions, benchmark results, and history from past sessions on this Pi. Use this when a question needs the user's own recorded history rather than general knowledge. When answering from the results, quote the passage text directly rather than paraphrasing it -- these are precise technical notes and paraphrasing risks changing the meaning.

function.name: weather_get_weather_summary
function.description: Get a combined weather overview for a location in a SINGLE call. Best for broad questions like "What's the weather like in Seattle?", "Is it safe to hike today?", or "Give me a weather rundown". Aggregates current conditions, forecast, and active alerts by default, and can also include air quality and lightning. Provide the location as coordinates (latitude+longitude), a saved location_name, or a free-text city_name. For a single specific data product (just the forecast, just alerts, etc.), call that specialized tool directly. Sections that are unavailable for a location (e.g. alerts in a country not yet covered) are noted rather than failing the whole summary.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location (-90 to 90). Not required if location_name or city_name is provided.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location (-180 to 180). Not required if location_name or city_name is provided.

location_name.description: Name of a saved location (e.g., "home", "cabin"). Use instead of coordinates to reference a saved location. List them with list_saved_locations.

city_name.description: Free-text place name to geocode (e.g., "Paris, France", "Bend, Oregon"). Use instead of coordinates when you only have a place name and it is not a saved location. Include state/country for disambiguation when possible.

include.description: Which sections to include (default: ["current", "forecast", "alerts"]). Add "air_quality" and/or "lightning" for a fuller picture.

days.description: Number of forecast days to include when the forecast section is requested (1-16, default: 7)

detail.description: Output verbosity: "summary" (shortest), "standard" (default, balanced), or "full" (everything the source provides, e.g. full alert descriptions, uncapped hourly forecast, embedded imagery).

units.description: Unit system for output: "imperial" (°F, mph, inHg) or "metric" (°C, km/h, hPa). Defaults to the server setting (imperial unless configured otherwise). Individual *_unit overrides below take precedence.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web and return a few current results with URLs and snippets.
